Flow Ramp Characterization: Non-Newtonian, Shear Thinning Behavior In slot-die coating, a slurry with a low-shear-rate viscosity (LSV) and lower high-shear-rate viscosity (HSV)is ideal. A high LSV promotes sharper edges while lower HSV values allow higher solids loading and faster coating rates. As shown in Figure 8, all slurries showed shear thinning behavior, which was more pronounced at higher solid contents. The viscosity trend follows: GDC>AFL>ASL, which is in agreement with the surface areas of the active materials. Figure 8 Dynamic viscosity curves indicating shear thinning behavior for all samples tested. Amplitude Sweep Experiment: Probing Liquid Network Strength The strength of the liquid network was characterized by measuring dependency of G’ and G’’ on strain. Within the LVR small micro cracks form, but network remains largely intact, outside of the LVR, however, macro fractures of network begin, and a 5% drop in moduli indicates the end of LVR. As shown in Figure 10, the storage modulus (G’) generally increases with increasing solid content. However, the G’ reduces when further increasing the solid content from 65% to 70% for the AFL and GDC. Figure 11 shows the phase angle, which reveals whether the slurries behave more like a solid or a liquid.
